name: BOTSWANA

flag.title: Flag of Botswana
flag.note: Blue for rain; black & white for the zebra

lead: Botswana is a sunny country in southern Africa with no coast. It has salt pans, huge herds of elephants, and a giant inland delta. It was very poor in 1966. Then it found diamonds and built schools and hospitals.

sections.geography: A sky full of salt & water
sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Botswana is almost flat. It is a giant plateau about 1,000 m above sea level. Around 70% of it is Kalahari, a dry land of golden grass and ancient dunes.
The Okavango River fans out into the world's largest inland delta. It covers 22,000 km² of channels and islands. The Makgadikgadi salt pans are a dried-up ancient lake that gleams white.
animals: Botswana has more elephants than any other country. 130,000 roam free. Herds wade into the Chobe River beside lions, hippos, and crocodiles. Parks cover nearly 40% of the land.
The zebra is the national animal. Its stripes inspired the colours of the flag. Tens of thousands migrate across the Makgadikgadi grasslands.
culture: The Tswana follow botho. It means you become a full person through kindness and community. Rushing past without a warm 'Dumela' (hello) is rude. Seswaa, pounded beef, is the national dish.
The kgotla is an open-air meeting under a tree. Every adult may speak. It settles disputes and shapes policy.
history: Botswana became independent on 30 Sept 1966. It was among the world's six poorest nations. It had just 12 km of paved roads and no universities. Eight months later, geologists struck diamonds.
The government put every pula of diamond money into schools, hospitals, and roads. Botswana then had the world's fastest economic growth for three decades. It never had a coup (army takeover).
wows: Botswana has 130,000 elephants, more than any other country.
The Okavango floods in the dry season, after rain falls in Angola.
The Sewelô diamond (2019) weighed 1,758 carats, the 2nd-largest ever found.
'Pula' means both 'rain' and 'cheers', and it names Botswana's money.
Chobe National Park holds up to 50,000 elephants.
The flat Makgadikgadi salt pans mirror the stars when wet.
Botswana reached 90%+ HIV treatment coverage in under a decade.

myths.fact: Diamonds form deep underground from pure carbon. Most are older than any plant.
Elephants suck water into the trunk, then squirt it into the mouth.
